questions.q: Which of the following is a requirement for creating an immutable class in Java?
options: Declare fields private and final and provide no setters
Provide public setters for all fields
questions.exp: Immutability requires that state cannot change after construction: private final fields and no mutators.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of compile-time (static) polymorphism?
options: Overriding a method of an abstract class
questions.exp: Overloaded calls are resolved by the compiler from the argument list; overriding is resolved at run time.

questions.q: Which of the following is true for an abstract class in Java?
options: It can contain both abstract and concrete methods but cannot be instantiated
It cannot contain any concrete method
It can be instantiated using new
questions.exp: An abstract class may mix abstract and implemented methods, but objects cannot be created from it directly.

questions.q: In Java, with Parent p = new Child(); p.show(); where show() is overridden in Child, which version runs?
options: Child's version, chosen at run time
Parent's version, chosen at compile time
questions.exp: Dynamic method dispatch uses the actual object type at run time.

questions.q: Which keyword is used to place a Java class into a package?
questions.exp: The package statement must be the first statement of the source file.

questions.q: A Java member with no access modifier (default access) is visible:
questions.exp: Default (package-private) access limits visibility to the same package.

questions.q: In Java, abstraction is achieved using:
questions.exp: Abstract classes and interfaces declare what is done while hiding how it is done.

questions.q: For class Derived : public Base, when an object of Derived is created, the constructors run in the order:
options: Order is decided at run time
questions.exp: Base sub-objects are constructed first, then the derived part.
f is virtual, so the call through the base pointer is bound at run time to B::f.

questions.q: Objects created with the new operator in Java are allocated in the:
questions.exp: All Java objects live on the heap; local primitive variables and references live on the thread stack.

questions.q: In C++, protected inheritance makes the public members of the base class ____ members of the derived class.
questions.exp: Under protected inheritance both public and protected base members become protected.

questions.q:
Statement I: A static data member of a C++ class is shared by all objects of the class.
Statement II: A static member function can use the this pointer to access the calling object.
Which is correct?
options: Statement I is false and Statement II is true
Statement I is true and Statement II is false
questions.exp: Static data is shared per class, but static functions have no this pointer.

questions.q: In a UML class diagram, a dashed line with a hollow triangular arrowhead pointing to an interface denotes:
questions.exp: Realization (implements) is drawn as a dashed line with a hollow triangle; generalization uses a solid line.

questions.q: Which design principle states that a class should have only one reason to change?
questions.exp: This is the S of SOLID: Single Responsibility.
Constructing x prints 1; passing x by value invokes the copy constructor, printing 2.

questions.q: Which technique resolves the ambiguity caused by the diamond problem in C++ multiple inheritance?
questions.exp: Declaring the common base as virtual ensures a single shared base sub-object.

questions.q: Why is the Java main method declared static?
options: So the JVM can call it without creating an object of the class
So it can access private members of other classes
So it is inherited by subclasses
questions.exp: The JVM invokes main before any object exists, so it must belong to the class.

questions.q: What is the default value of an int instance variable in Java?
questions.exp: Instance variables get default values; int defaults to 0.

questions.q: A static member function in C++ can directly access:
options: Only static data members and other static member functions
questions.exp: A static function belongs to the class, has no this pointer, and so can directly use only static members.

questions.q: The relationship 'a Car has an Engine' where the engine cannot exist without the car is best modelled as:
questions.exp: A strong has-a relationship with dependent lifetime is composition.

questions.q: In C++, the copy constructor is invoked when:
options: An object is passed by reference to a function
An object is passed by value to a function
A pointer to an object is declared
questions.exp: Passing by value creates a copy of the argument, calling the copy constructor.

questions.q: Which modifier, applied to a Java class, prevents it from being extended?
questions.exp: A final class cannot have subclasses; abstract classes exist precisely to be extended.
The implicit super() call runs the parent constructor first.

questions.q: A try-with-resources statement in Java requires the resource class to implement:
questions.exp: Resources declared in the try header must implement AutoCloseable (or Closeable) so close() is called automatically.

questions.q: How many arguments does an overloaded binary operator take when defined as a member function of a class?
questions.exp: The left operand is the invoking object, so only the right operand is passed as an argument.

questions.q: Which statement is correct about method overriding in Java?
options: The overriding method must have a different parameter list
The overriding method may be private when the original is public
The overriding method cannot have a more restrictive access modifier
The call is resolved at compile time
questions.exp: Overriding must keep the same signature and cannot reduce visibility; dispatch is at run time.

questions.q: In Java, the finally block:
options: Executes only when an exception is thrown
Executes whether or not an exception occurs
Executes only when no exception occurs
Cannot be used without a catch block
questions.exp: finally is meant for clean-up and runs in both normal and exceptional flow (and may follow try alone).

questions.q: In C++, memory allocated with new int[10] must be released using:
questions.exp: Array allocations made by new[] are released with delete[].

questions.q: Which change alone does NOT allow two Java methods in the same class to be overloaded?
options: Changing the type of a parameter
Changing the order of parameters of different types
questions.exp: Overloading requires different parameter lists; a different return type alone causes a compile-time error.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT inherited by a derived class in C++?
questions.exp: Constructors (and destructors, assignment operators, friends) are not inherited.

questions.q: Which is the correct way to start a function template declaration in C++?
questions.exp: Function templates begin with template <class T> (or template <typename T>) before the function.
A long cannot be narrowed to int but widens to double, so f(double) is chosen.

questions.q: Which Thread method makes the calling thread wait until the thread on which it is invoked terminates?
questions.exp: t.join() blocks the caller until t finishes.
1+2 is evaluated first as an int (3) and then appended: A3.

questions.q: Making the constructor of a C++ class private prevents:
options: Creating objects of the class from outside the class
questions.exp: Only members or friends can then construct objects; this is used in the Singleton pattern.

questions.q: The Liskov Substitution Principle states that:
options: Objects of a subclass should be usable wherever objects of the superclass are expected without breaking correctness
A class should depend on abstractions, not concrete classes
A class should have a single responsibility
Clients should not depend on interfaces they do not use
questions.exp: LSP requires subtypes to be substitutable for their base types.

questions.q: Which package of Java is imported automatically into every program?
questions.exp: java.lang (String, Object, System, Math) is implicitly imported.

questions.q: The default copy constructor of a C++ class performs:
questions.exp: The compiler-generated copy constructor copies each member, so pointer members are copied by address (shallow copy).
char is promoted to int (a promotion), which is preferred over conversion to double.

questions.q: In Java, an interface can:
questions.exp: An interface may extend any number of other interfaces.
s becomes JAVA; the character at index 2 is V.

questions.q: A friend function of a C++ class:
options: Is a member function of the class
Is not a member of the class but can access its private members
questions.exp: Friendship grants access to private and protected members without making the function a member; it is not inherited.
r is a reference (alias) of x, so r++ increments x to 6.

questions.q:
Statement I: An abstract class in Java may have no abstract methods.
Statement II: An object of an abstract class can be created with new if it has a public constructor.
Which is correct?
options: Statement I is true and Statement II is false
Statement I is false and Statement II is true
questions.exp: An abstract class can be declared without abstract methods, but it can never be instantiated directly.

questions.q: Which UML diagram is used to show the interaction between objects arranged in time order?
questions.exp: A sequence diagram shows messages exchanged between objects along a vertical time axis.

questions.q: What does "Hello".substring(1, 3) return in Java?
questions.exp: substring(begin, end) returns characters from index 1 up to index 2, i.e. el.

questions.q: What happens if run() is called directly on a Thread object instead of start()?
options: The body of run() executes in the calling thread like an ordinary method
questions.exp: Only start() creates a new thread of execution; run() alone is a normal method call.

questions.q: Which is the correct declaration of a pure virtual function in C++?
questions.exp: A pure virtual function is declared with = 0 after the declarator.
Each add returns *this, so x becomes 2+3+4 = 9.
A stack is LIFO; after popping 3 the top is 2.

questions.q: A static initialisation block in a Java class is executed:
options: Once, when the class is loaded
Every time an object is created
Every time a static method is called
Only when the class is serialised
questions.exp: static blocks run once at class initialisation time.
m() runs first and its finally block prints F before the returned value 1 is printed.

questions.q: Classes B and C both derive directly from class A. This type of inheritance is:
questions.exp: Several classes inheriting from one base form hierarchical inheritance.
append gives abcd and reverse turns it into dcba.

questions.q: Which statement about HashMap in Java is correct?
options: It does not allow null values
It maintains elements in sorted order
questions.exp: HashMap permits one null key and many null values; it is unsynchronised and unordered.
After pop_back the vector is {10,20}: size 2 and last element 20, printing 220.

questions.q: The Open/Closed principle states that software entities should be:
options: Open for extension but closed for modification
Open for modification but closed for extension
Open to all users and closed to none
Closed to inheritance and open to composition
questions.exp: New behaviour should be added by extending, not by editing existing, tested code.

questions.q: A C++ class becomes an abstract class when it:
options: Has at least one pure virtual function
questions.exp: Any class with a pure virtual function cannot be instantiated and is abstract.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT an advantage of encapsulation?
options: Control over how data is modified
Guaranteed faster execution of every program
Freedom to change internal implementation without affecting users
questions.exp: Encapsulation improves safety and maintainability; it does not guarantee speed.

questions.q: Which of the following is a marker interface in Java?
questions.exp: Serializable declares no methods and only marks classes whose objects can be serialised.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Constructors cannot be virtual in C++.
Reason (R): The virtual-table pointer is set up during construction, so the virtual mechanism is not available before the object exists.
options: Both A and R are true and R is not the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.exp: Dynamic dispatch needs the vptr, which the constructor itself initialises, so a virtual constructor is meaningless.

questions.q: A C++ member function declared as void show() const; promises that it:
options: Will not modify the data members of the object
questions.exp: A const member function cannot change the object's non-mutable data members.
s1 and s2 refer to the same pooled literal; new String creates a separate object, so == gives false for s3.
a = 10 + (10 + 12): a++ yields 10 (a becomes 11), ++a yields 12, so a = 10 + 22 = 32.
maxv(3,7) gives 7 and maxv(2.5,1.5) gives 2.5; no separator is printed, so 72.5.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a recognised type of inheritance in OOP?
questions.exp: Single, multiple, multilevel, hierarchical and hybrid are standard types; circular inheritance is illegal.

questions.q: Which keyword is used in Java to inherit a class from another class?
questions.exp: A class inherits another class using extends; implements is used for interfaces.

questions.q:
Statement I: Method overloading is resolved at compile time.
Statement II: Method overriding is resolved at run time.
Which is correct?
questions.exp: Overloads are chosen by the compiler from the signatures; overridden methods are chosen by the object's actual type at run time.

questions.q: In a UML class diagram, a line ending in a hollow (unfilled) diamond represents:
questions.exp: Hollow diamond is aggregation (weak has-a); a filled diamond is composition.

questions.q: In C++, what happens when an exception is thrown and no matching catch handler is found?
options: A default handler prints the message and continues
std::terminate is called and the program ends abnormally
questions.exp: An unhandled exception leads to std::terminate (which calls abort by default).

questions.q: When a subclass defines a static method with the same signature as a static method in its superclass, this is called:
questions.exp: Static methods are not overridden; the subclass method hides the superclass one.

questions.q: Which statement about the Error class in Java (for example OutOfMemoryError) is correct?
options: It is a checked exception that must be declared
It is a subclass of Exception
It represents serious problems that applications are not expected to handle
questions.exp: Errors are unchecked and indicate serious JVM or system level problems.

questions.q: In Java, the super keyword is used to refer to:
questions.exp: super refers to the immediate superclass's members and constructors.

questions.q: Interfaces in C++ are typically implemented using:
options: Abstract classes whose member functions are all pure virtual
questions.exp: C++ has no interface keyword; a class with only pure virtual functions serves as an interface.

questions.q: Which of the following can access a protected member of a base class in C++?
options: Only the base class, not derived classes
Member functions of the derived classes and of the base class itself
Only objects of the base class created in main
questions.exp: Protected members are accessible inside the class and in classes derived from it.

questions.q: Which declaration creates a vector of 5 integers each initialised to 7?
questions.exp: The constructor vector<int>(n, value) creates n copies of value.

questions.q: In a UML class diagram, the multiplicity 1..* on an association end means:
questions.exp: 1..* means at least one and possibly many.

questions.q: Why can a Java class achieve a form of multiple inheritance through interfaces?
options: A class can implement more than one interface
A class can extend two interfaces
questions.exp: A class may implement any number of interfaces, thereby inheriting several types.

questions.q: The synchronized keyword in Java is used to:
options: Allow only one thread at a time to execute a critical section guarded by the same lock
questions.exp: synchronized provides mutual exclusion on an object's monitor.

questions.q: Which of the following cannot be overridden in Java?
questions.exp: The final modifier forbids overriding.
show is not virtual, so the call is bound statically to the pointer type A.

questions.q: Which of the following is possible in a Java abstract class but NOT in a Java 8 interface?
questions.exp: Abstract classes can declare constructors (called through subclass constructors); interfaces cannot.

questions.q: In C++, which data members must be initialised using a constructor member initializer list?
questions.exp: const and reference members cannot be assigned later, so they must be initialised in the initializer list.
g() is inherited from B but calls the virtual f(), which dispatches to D::f on a D object.

questions.q: Which statement about a constructor in C++ is correct?
options: It has the same name as its class and no return type
It must return an int value
questions.exp: A constructor carries the class name and has no return type (not even void); it cannot be static or virtual.
x refers to B's field (20) and super.x to A's field (10).

questions.q: CRC cards used in object-oriented design stand for:
questions.exp: A CRC card lists a class, its responsibilities and the collaborating classes.

questions.q: In Java, the throws clause is used to:
options: Declare in a method signature the exceptions it may pass to its caller
questions.exp: throws lists exceptions a method may propagate; throw raises one.

questions.q: In C++, when a class is derived using private inheritance, the public members of the base class become ____ members of the derived class.
questions.exp: Private inheritance makes all accessible base members (public and protected) private in the derived class.
Arrays are objects and b is another reference to the same array, so a[0] is 9.

questions.q: Which UML diagram models the different states of an object during its life and the events causing transitions?
questions.exp: State machine (state chart) diagrams show states and transitions of an object.

questions.q: For class C : public A, public B, when an object of C is created the constructors execute in the order:
questions.exp: Base classes are constructed in the order of their declaration in the derivation list, then the derived class.

questions.q: Encapsulation in OOP means:
options: Deriving a new class from an existing class
Using one name for many different forms
Showing only the essential features to the user
Binding data and the functions that operate on it into one unit and restricting direct access to the data
questions.exp: Encapsulation wraps data and methods together in a class and controls access to the data using access specifiers.
After p += 2, *p is 30 and *a is 10, so the result is 20.

questions.q: Which design pattern ensures that a class has only one instance and provides a global access point to it?
questions.exp: Singleton restricts instantiation to a single object.

questions.q: If a Java class contains an abstract method, then the class must be:
questions.exp: A class with at least one abstract method must itself be declared abstract.

questions.q: The size of the char data type in Java is:
questions.exp: Java char is a 16-bit unsigned Unicode (UTF-16) value.

questions.q: Which class is the root of the class hierarchy in Java?
questions.exp: Every class implicitly extends java.lang.Object.

questions.q: The Java compiler (javac) translates source code into:
options: Native machine code of the host CPU
Object code specific to the operating system
questions.exp: javac produces platform-independent bytecode (.class files), which the JVM interprets or JIT-compiles.

questions.q: Java does not allow a class to extend more than one class mainly to avoid:
options: Ambiguity such as the diamond problem
questions.exp: Two parents providing the same member would create ambiguity.

questions.q: Which statement about interfaces in Java 8 is correct?
options: They cannot contain any method body
They can contain default methods with a body
questions.exp: Java 8 allows default and static methods with bodies in interfaces; no constructors or instance fields.

questions.q: Why should the destructor of a polymorphic base class in C++ be declared virtual?
options: To ensure the derived destructor runs when an object is deleted through a base pointer
questions.exp: Without a virtual destructor, deleting a derived object via a base pointer is undefined behaviour and skips the derived destructor.

questions.q: In Java, an overriding method returning a subclass of the original return type is allowed. This feature is called:
questions.exp: Since Java 5 an overriding method may narrow its return type; this is a covariant return type.

questions.q: Given that Shape is a Java interface, which statement causes a compile-time error?
questions.exp: An interface cannot be instantiated directly; arrays of an interface type and null references are fine.

questions.q: Which declaration uses an unbounded wildcard in Java generics?
questions.exp: The ? symbol is the unbounded wildcard type argument.
Two constructions print CC; at the end of main both are destroyed printing DD.

questions.q: Which C++ STL container stores unique elements in sorted order?
questions.exp: set keeps unique keys ordered (usually a balanced tree).
c is shared by all objects; three constructor calls make it 3.
null matches both overloads; the compiler picks the most specific type, String.

questions.q: The JIT (Just-In-Time) compiler of the JVM:
options: Converts frequently executed bytecode to native machine code at run time
Converts Java source code to bytecode
Removes unused classes from the heap
Checks bytecode for syntax errors before execution
questions.exp: JIT compiles hot spots to native code at run time to improve speed.
Fields are resolved by reference type (A) while methods are dispatched on the object type (B): AB.

questions.q: A member of a Java class declared protected is accessible:
options: Within its package and by subclasses in other packages
questions.exp: protected gives package access plus access through inheritance in other packages.
Java evaluates left to right: i++ gives 1 (i becomes 2), so j = 1*2 + 2 = 4.

questions.q: Which of the following is a checked exception in Java?
questions.exp: IOException is checked and must be caught or declared; the others are RuntimeExceptions.

questions.q: Immediately after start() is called on a new Java Thread object, the thread is in the ____ state.
questions.exp: start() moves a thread from New to Runnable, where it waits for CPU scheduling.

questions.q: Two interfaces in Java declare the same default method and a class implements both. The code compiles only if:
options: The compiler is left to choose the first interface
One of the interfaces is declared final
questions.exp: The conflict must be resolved by overriding the method in the implementing class.
Static blocks run parent then child (1,4); then parent instance block and constructor (2,3), then child (5,6).
Division by zero skips A, the catch prints B, finally prints C, then execution continues with D.

questions.q: Which of the following operators cannot be overloaded in C++?
questions.exp: The scope resolution operator :: (along with . .* ?: sizeof) cannot be overloaded.
The overloaded + adds the x members: 3 + 4 = 7.

questions.q: In object-oriented analysis, identifying candidate classes by underlining nouns in the requirement description belongs to:
questions.exp: Noun-verb analysis of the requirements is a classic analysis technique to find classes and operations.
Three objects are constructed and n is never decremented, so n is 3.

questions.q: In Java, if a superclass has only a parameterised constructor, then every subclass constructor must:
options: Do nothing special; the compiler supplies default values
Explicitly call super(arguments) as its first statement
questions.exp: No default superclass constructor exists, so the implicit super() would fail; an explicit super(args) call is needed.

questions.q: When a C++ try block is followed by catch handlers for both a base exception class and its derived class, the correct order is:
questions.exp: Handlers are tried in order; a base handler first would catch derived exceptions and hide the derived handler.

questions.q: Which statement about C++ destructors is correct?
options: A class can have several overloaded destructors
A destructor can take one int parameter
A destructor has no parameters and cannot be overloaded
A destructor must always be called explicitly
questions.exp: A destructor is written ~ClassName(), takes no arguments and has no return type, so only one exists per class.

questions.q: Which relationship is best modelled using inheritance?
questions.exp: Inheritance models an is-a relationship.

questions.q: Which method of the Thread class is used to begin execution of a new thread in Java?
questions.exp: start() creates a new call stack and invokes run() in it.

questions.q:
Match the UML diagram with its use:
1. Class diagram  2. Sequence diagram  3. Use case diagram  4. Deployment diagram
P. Static structure of classes  Q. Order of messages between objects  R. Functional requirements and actors  S. Hardware nodes and software placed on them
questions.exp: Class diagram shows structure, sequence diagram message order, use case diagram requirements, deployment diagram physical nodes.

questions.q: Which STL container stores its elements in contiguous memory and supports random access with operator[]?
questions.exp: vector stores elements contiguously like an array and supports O(1) indexing.

questions.q: Autoboxing in Java refers to:
options: Automatic conversion of a primitive value to its wrapper object
Automatic conversion of an object to a string
Packing several classes in a package
questions.exp: For example int to Integer is done by the compiler automatically.
Strings are immutable; concat returns a new String that is discarded, so s remains Hi.
The thrown value is an int, so the catch(int) handler matches before the catch-all handler: it prints int 10.

questions.q:
Match the C++ feature with its purpose:
1. Virtual function  2. Friend function  3. Static member  4. Template
P. Generic programming  Q. Access to private members from outside the class  R. Data shared by all objects  S. Run-time polymorphism
questions.exp: Virtual gives run-time polymorphism, friend allows private access, static is shared, template gives generics.

questions.q: Why does the declaration List<int> fail to compile in Java?
options: Type arguments must be reference types, so Integer must be used
questions.exp: Generics do not accept primitives; wrapper types such as Integer are used instead.

questions.q: In a UML use case diagram, an actor represents:
options: An external entity that interacts with the system
questions.exp: Actors are users or external systems that interact with the system under study.

questions.q: In a non-static member function of a C++ class, the this pointer points to:
options: The object on which the function was invoked
The base class of the current class
The first member of the class
questions.exp: this holds the address of the invoking (current) object.
Key a is overwritten, so the map has 2 entries and m[a] is 3: output 23.
x prints 00, y prints 50, z prints 12, giving 005012.

questions.q: In Java, variables declared inside an interface are implicitly:
questions.exp: Interface fields are constants: public, static and final.
